content:
Running Lean code from untrusted sources is potentially dangerous, just as for any programming language.

bubble provides a simple tool for creating VSCode sessions for Lean projects, encapsulated in a system level sandbox (Incus containers on Linux, wrapped via Colima on macOS).

# Install
uv tool install git+https://github.com/kim-em/bubble.git

# Open a bubble for a GitHub PR — just paste the URL, and you get a containerized VSCode window, with Lean installed and a warm cache!
bubble https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/35219

There are many additional features, including:

  • shell access into the bubble
  • running bubbles on remote or cloud machines, using VSCode remote sessions
  • prepared images with baked-in VSCode server / Lean toolchains --- first launch is slow, but faster afterwards
  • shared Mathlib cache between bubbles
  • your GitHub auth token never enters the bubble: git access is mediated by a proxy
  • customizable security posture

I've been using it successfully for a while, and would be happy to have user feedback. It is intentionally opinionated, so bubble definitely "gets in your way" sometimes, and not all workflows will work well inside bubble.

It's tested on Linux and macOS. It may work on Windows, under WSL :woman_shrugging:.

bubble is also useful for encapsulating AI agents working in YOLO mode, and supports installing coding agents inside the bubble, and injecting AI access tokens.

If you become aware of security flaws in the bubble model not already described in Security limitations please let me know!
